strategy.summary: Kettle & Co. has no smoke tests. Add a small Playwright smoke suite (tests/smoke/shop.spec.js), each test tagged @smoke, that checks the shop's critical paths through the configured baseURL using only GET requests and the browser-side cart cookie: the health endpoint, the catalogue, a product page, the cart and the checkout page. No test places an order (POST /orders, the only server write).
inScope: Catalogue home page lists every product with its price
Product page reached from the catalogue shows name, price and an Add to cart button
Adding to the cart (a browser cookie only) shows the line and total on the cart page
Checkout page shows the order form for a non-empty cart, without submitting it
outOfScope: Placing an order (POST /orders): it writes data on the server, so it stays with tests/checkout.spec.js
Order confirmation page: it needs an order that only placing one creates
Validation, empty states, 404 and error paths (fuller suite)
assumptions: Adding to the cart only sets a cookie in the test's own browser context (public/app.js) and sends no request to the server, so it counts as read-only for the deployed build.

The product list comes from src/catalogue.js PRODUCTS, which is shipped code, not seeded data, so every environment built from the same commit shows it; tests import PRODUCTS and formatPrice rather than copying them.

The suite reaches the app only through Playwright's baseURL (BASE_URL or the local default in playwright.config.js); no first-party service is faked. Locally the config's webServer starts the real shop.
The shop has no sign-in, so no credentials are needed.

risks.description: A smoke test accidentally writes data on production (submits the checkout form).
risks.mitigation: Checkout case only asserts the form is shown; it never clicks Place order. Only GET requests are made.
Assertions use PRODUCTS imported from the shipped catalogue rather than test-only seed data.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The app is up: GET /health through the base URL answers 200 with status ok.
A user can reach the catalogue and see every product with its price.
A user can open a product page from the catalogue and see its name, price and Add to cart button.
A user can add a product to the cart and see it with the right total on the cart page.
A user with items in the cart can reach the checkout page and see the order form.
Every smoke test is tagged @smoke in its title, reaches the app only through the base URL, and makes no request that creates, changes or deletes server data.
acceptanceCriteria.metBy: Each test in tests/smoke/shop.spec.js has @smoke in its title, uses relative paths against Playwright's baseURL, and issues only GET navigations/requests; no form is submitted.

testCases.title: health endpoint reports the shop is up @smoke
testCases.rationale: Critical path: the build starts and answers at all.

testCases.title: catalogue lists every product with its price @smoke
steps: For each product in PRODUCTS check its link and price in its list item
testCases.expected: Heading shown; each product's link with exact name and its formatted price shown
testCases.rationale: Critical path: the home page and catalogue render.

testCases.title: product page opens from the catalogue with its price and Add to cart @smoke
testCases.expected: URL /products/teapot, heading 'Cast-iron teapot', price £48.00, Add to cart button visible
testCases.rationale: Critical path: product pages are reachable from the catalogue.

testCases.title: cart shows a product added from its page with the total @smoke
steps: Check status 'Added to your cart' and link 'Cart (1)'
testCases.expected: Cart page heading 'Your cart', a row for Cast-iron teapot, total £48.00
testCases.rationale: Critical path: the cart works (cookie only; no server write).

testCases.title: checkout page shows the order form for a filled cart @smoke
testCases.expected: Heading 'Checkout', total £18.00, Name/Email/Address fields and 'Place order' button visible; the form is not submitted
testCases.rationale: Critical path: users can reach checkout; placing the order is left out because it writes data.

strategy.environmentNotes: Run with `npm run test:e2e -- --grep @smoke`; set BASE_URL to target a deployed build, otherwise playwright.config.js starts the shop on localhost:4175. Needs `npx playwright install chromium`.

refusals.reason: tests/smoke/shop.spec.js written before testforge:api, testforge:playwright, testforge:implementation were loaded
`playwright` runs tests, and this run writes a smoke suite for http://host.docker.internal:62147, which isn't marked disposable, without running it.

candidates.text: When a run targets a non-disposable deployed build, run_command refuses any playwright invocation (even `--list`); verify by reading the code plus run_checks, self_check and review. The repo has no lint/typecheck scripts, so run_checks reports nothing to check.
candidates.evidence: GAPS-20261122-E4E2: run_command `npx playwright test --list --grep @smoke` refused; run_checks: "No repository checks apply to the changed files."
